Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

presence noun

also in the presence of, in my presence, in front of (someone), presence of mind, be present, face to face, be face to face with

classical

Cic. Att. 4.4.1: cētera cōram agēmus
Ov. F. 5.69–70: cōram sene
Traupman 236, 319
Traupman 319

cōram

adverb; and preposition with the ablative

in the presence of, before; in person, face to face

As a preposition, before a person’s eyes (cōram patre); as an adverb, in person, face to face, as against by letter: Cicero ends letters with it.

Other words

  • praesēns, praesentis — present, in person; mē praesente, in my presence

    participle of praesum, as an adjective; often in the ablative absolute · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.12.2: praesentem audīre mālō · Declension on Wiktionary

    Latin puts the person in the ablative absolute where English uses the abstract noun: mē praesente, in my presence; the opposite is mē absente (see absence).

  • praesentia, praesentiae f. — presence, being there

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.8.5: dēsīderium praesentiae tuae (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.G. 5.43.4: praesentia animī, presence of mind (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The noun is classical but less used than the two above. In praesentiā means “for the present, now” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • cētera cōram agēmus

    we’ll deal with the rest face to faceCic. Att. 4.4.1

  • quid, cum cōram sumus et garrīmus quicquid in buccam?

    and what about when we are together and chatter whatever comes into our heads?Cic. Att. 12.1.2

  • verba quis audēret cōram sene digna rubōre dīcere?

    who would have dared to say words to make one blush in front of an old man?Ov. F. 5.69–70

  • praesentem audīre mālō

    I’d rather hear it from you in personCic. Att. 2.12.2

  • adsum praesēns praesentī tibi

    here I am, face to face with youPlaut. Ps. 5.1.27 (Lewis & Short)

  • Praesēns praesentī tibi esse.

    To be face to face with you.Traupman 312

See also absence, personal, attend, I’m here, in front of.
